section_summary.extract_value: This section is an introduction to a study on Black female body image and obesity. It discusses how contemporary sociocultural shifts—including increased media visibility of thin Black female celebrities, heightened public health obesity prevention initiatives, and escalating weight discrimination—may be creating a 'new era' in Black females' body image experiences, potentially narrowing historical Black-White differences in body dissatisfaction. The section argues that overweight and obese Black young women may be particularly vulnerable to negative body image effects and weight-related stress, especially during the developmental transition to college, and calls for further research on positive body image coping resources in this population.
